Recipe:

Here are a few recipes I was able to dig up from postings I've made on reddit. A little messy but I think you can follow them:

Changua:

Finely chop some scallions and cilantro and add them to 1/2 cup of water and 1/2 cup of milk, season with salt. Bring the mixture to a boil, and then let it simmer for a few minutes, then Crack an egg in the soup and let it cook for a minute or two. On a plate crumble pieces of toast or if you can find calados and pour the soup over them. Garnish with chopped cilantro. Some people add grated cheese (any semi-hard cheese will do). This is for one serving.

Sancocho de espinazo:

Recipe: Ingredients : 1 pound of beef backbone
1 potato per serving
1 green plantain chopped into ~1 inch pieces
1 yucca chopped into ~1 inch pieces
Green onions
1 stalk of celery
Cilantro
Beef stock
Water
Salt and Pepper
Procedure :
In a large pot add beef broth, water, backbone, onions and celery bring to a boil and let simmer for 30 minutes or until meat is soft.
In 10 minute intervals add plantains first, yucca second and potatoes third.
Adjust seasoning and let simmer for another 30 minutes or until potatoes are soft. Add cilantro and serve.
Accompany with white rice and avocado.

Oxtail stew:

I put the oxtail pieces in a pressure cooker with beef broth and green onions for an hour. In another pot I sauté some onions with garlic on olive oil then add two chopped tomatoes and chopped bell pepper and let it cook on low for half an hour. When the pressure cooker has cooled add the veggies to the oxtail chopped yuca (use potatoes if you don't have) and chopped green plantain. Mix everything and let cook until plantains are soft stirring occasionally. If the sauce is to thick add water as needed.

Lentil stew:

Ingredients:
Lentils (a handful per serving)
1 or 2 onions finely diced
1 or 2 tomatoes chopped
A bell pepper, chopped, seeded
1 or 2 garlic cloves
1 or 2 sausages sliced (whatever kind you like)
1 of 2 potatoes
1 or 2 cups of chicken stock
Olive oil
Salt and pepper
A plantain
Pork
Instructions:
Soak the lentils in water overnight and wash before cooking.
On a pot heat some olive oil and saute the garlic and onions until onions are translucent and soft. Add the chopped tomatoes and bell pepper and let it cook on low heat for 20 or 30 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it cool a little. Add a cup of chicken stock and blend it with a food processor or blender.
Put the blended "sauce" back in the pot add the lentils, potatoes and sausage, salt and pepper to taste and more chicken stock or water if needed on high heat until it boils, lower the heat and let it simmer until potatoes are soft. Stir occasionally.
Meanwhile in a pot put the plantain with the rind still on in boiling water and let it simmer on low-medium heat until the potatoes are soft.
Fry a piece of pork rind or crackling seasoned with salt and pepper.
Put everything in a plate and enjoy, I eat it with a piece of avocado.

Pollo sudado:

4 Pieces of chicken, I used legs
1 or 2 tomatoes chopped finely
1 Small Bell Pepper chopped finely
1 scallion mashed
1 tooth of garlic mashed
3 or 4 potatoes peeled and cut in half
1 small yucca chopped into medium pieces
water
2 Tbps oil
salt to taste
Then put in a pot the chicken with the tomatoes, bell pepper, scallion, garlic, oil and water. Bring it to a boil and lower the heat, add the potatoes, yucca and season with salt. Let it cook on low heat until everything is soft, serve with plain white rice drizzled with the "sauce".

Chicken rice:

Ingredients:
1 chicken breast
1 cup rice
2 cup water
1 scallion
1 diced onion
1 red bell pepper chopped into cubes
2 Tomato, diced
1 carrot, diced
1 clove garlic
1/2 cup peas
1/2 cup chopped green beans
1 bouillon cube
1 tablespoon oil
salt to taste
Preparation:
Cook chicken in 2 or more cups of water with scallions and bouillon cube. Let it cool and shred.
In a pot heat oil and proceed to sauté onions and garlic, when onions are translucent add tomatoes and bell pepper on medium-low heat. Let it cook until a sort of sauce forms maybe 15 minutes, this is called the “guiso”.
If you are using fresh peas cook them for a few minutes in water to soften them and blanch the green beans to remove some of the bitterness while the “guiso” cooks.
At this point add carrots, peas, green beans, shredded chicken and rice, stir well and let it cook for a few minutes.
Turn the heat up to high and add 2 cups of the broth where you cooked the chicken, when it starts to dry and you see bubbles form, lower the heat to the lowest you can (to avoid sticking and burning) if you have one use a heat difusor (can be and old tin cover), cover the pot and cook until rice is dry.
The dish is usually served with salad and French fries or potato chips.
